examples.name: Cosmic Gems arc (SPT0615-JD1)
examples.age_scope: Approximate cosmic age of this strongly lensed observed system
observed_features: Dense, compact star-forming clusters are resolved inside a young galaxy.
The observed chain and mirrored image are altered by strong gravitational lensing.
limitations: The five detected clusters are specific to this observation, not a required number in each conceptual galaxy.
Do not render the stretched arc or mirrored copies as the intrinsic galaxy structure.

source.label: ESA/Webb: Star clusters in the Cosmic Gems arc (2024)

examples.name: Firefly Sparkle and companions
examples.age_scope: Approximate cosmic age of the observed galaxy
observed_features: Compact luminous star clusters lie within diffuse, asymmetric galactic light.
Nearby companions may influence later assembly; the eventual shape cannot be predicted from this example.
limitations: The lensed observation and the separately labelled artist reconstruction are distinct products.
Companions are observed; a merger trajectory, tidal distortion and deterministic future morphology are not measured here.

source.label: NASA Webb: Firefly Sparkle and companions (2024)

examples.name: CEERS observed projected shape examples
examples.age_scope: Broad cosmic-age range of the study sample, not an individual age for every pictured object
observed_features: Elongated, flattened, disk-like and compact spherical appearances occur within the study sample.
Apparent two-dimensional shape and model-inferred three-dimensional geometry are different quantities.
limitations: Published sample fractions are not used as scene family probabilities or universal population fractions.
The sample range does not date the beginning of disk or spheroid formation.

source.label: NASA Webb: CEERS distant-galaxy shape diversity (2024)

examples.name: REBELS-25
examples.age_scope: Approximate cosmic age of this observed rotating-disc example
observed_features: ALMA gas kinematics establish an early strongly rotating disc.
Suggested bar and spiral structure are tentative and require more observations.
limitations: A gas intensity/velocity map is not an optical stellar surface map.
The conceptual early disc has no source-claimed measured bar or grand-design spiral arms.
This exceptional observed system does not establish that all galaxies have orderly discs at this age.

examples.name: ZS7 galaxy merger system
examples.age_scope: Approximate cosmic age of this observed interacting system
observed_features: JWST imaging and spectroscopy provide evidence for an ongoing merger of two galaxies hosting massive black holes.
The system provides an early example of assembly through galaxy interactions.
limitations: The scene's pair separation, tidal geometry and motion are illustrative, not fits to this system.
This is evidence for ongoing galaxy assembly, not a direct observation of completed black-hole coalescence or gravitational waves.

source.label: ESA/Webb: ZS7 ongoing galaxy merger evidence (2024)

examples.name: Later galaxy assembly and coexisting forms
examples.age_scope: Broad qualitative evolution context, not a dated transition or exclusive late-time population
observed_features: Modern spiral and elliptical systems developed through varied assembly histories.
Irregular, clumpy and interacting systems continue to exist; merging and assembly also occur today.
limitations: Later conceptual families overlap rather than all replacing early forms on one date.
No present-day catalog galaxy is identified as the future descendant of a scene node.

visual_policy.early_disk_display_before_example: Not adopted by this conservative visual guide; this is not a physical exclusion at earlier ages.

limitations: Observed examples illustrate diversity; they are not a census or an age-dependent morphology fraction.
A source's approximate observation age is not a first-appearance date, a universal transition, or the age of every galaxy in an illustrative scene.
The scene's 35 nodes, seeds, family assignments, colors, sizes and individual morph timings are display assumptions, not measured objects or evolutionary tracks.
Projected light, observing wavelength, resolution and gravitational lensing affect observed shapes; a lensed arc is not the intrinsic shape of a galaxy.
Early rotating discs exist; REBELS-25's proposed bar and spiral arms require further confirmation and are not adopted as measured structures.
Nearby spirals, spheroids, irregular and interacting galaxies coexist; no single final shape or deterministic evolution is prescribed.
Original chronology stages, current catalog coordinates, JPL model time and SPHEREx observations remain unchanged.
Reference observation pages are linked; the renderer is a conceptual code illustration, not a copied observation or a reconstruction of the past sky.
